newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia oppn challenges Fischer on shares.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia oppn challenges Fischer on shares.

text.p: Australian Labor opposition leader Kim Beazley said on Wednesday Trade Minister Tim Fischer should have disposed of a shareholding if he had taken ministerial action in relation to the company.
"It would be impractical for him (to hold the shares and act in relation to the company) and therefore he should have got rid of his shares immediately," Beazley told Sydney radio 2UE.
"It's not the point that you don't own shares. It's the point that you don't have a vested interest in any particular decision," Beazley said.
Fischer's share portfolio has included the Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd, whose interests have been promoted overseas by the government.
Beazley said if Fischer as a trade minister was actively involved in or about to take an action associated with a company he should have placed the action in somebody else's hands.

"If in fact you have a shareholding of such significance that that becomes impractical and that the decisions that you are going to take are obviously going to benefit then the best thing for you to do would be to dispense with those shares," he said.

The Australian Financial Review newspaper on Wednesday reported that Fischer appeared to be in breach of ministerial guidelines by owning shares in major mining and exporting companies over the last few months but had sold the shares.
Beazley said he wanted to know when Fischer had sold the shares and what sort of decisions may have been associated with any company in which he had been involved.
The newspaper reported that Fischer had sold some shares as recently as last week.
It also reported that Finance Minister John Fahey had failed to declare ownership of some shares in the pecuniary interest register for members of parliament.
Beazley said the opposition had not been pursuing Fahey.
"But if there is a matter of interest of course we will take an interest in it," Beazley said.
The conflict of interest share row has already claimed the resignations of Assistant Treasurer Jim Short on Sunday and Parliamentary Secretary to the Treasurer Senator Brian Gibson on Tuesday.
